title: Cleo Brown and the girl piano-singer trend
summary: Cleo Brown's records began a trend for girl pianist-singers, and people expected Nellie to sing when she reached California.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And you mentioned -- well, that was later on in L.A., you mentioned a lady named Cleo Brown in L.A.

Cleo Brown was very popular when I first came to California. You see, she -- before I left Louisiana, as a matter of fact, she was, you know, just -- she had made a record called, 'It's a Heavenly Thing,' and this -- she sort of started the trend really for girl piano players, you know, piano players and vocalists. She started this trend.

And she was just -- oh, as I say, when I got here, Cleo Brown, that's all you could hear, Cleo Brown. Cleo Brown. She was from Chicago. And when I came out here I think that was the one thing that, you know, made people -- you know, every time they'd see a girl piano player they'd expect you to sing. Well, I really didn't concentrate on singing, as I said before. I always played, you know, because I had been playing for a long time, and I played and was used to playing with orchestras. And when I came out here, well of course when you go into a thing where you are vocalizing, and see this is a whole different bag. It is, it's absolutely completely different, and I really had not -- this was far from my mind, it really was, it was very far from my mind. I was thinking when I got out to California what I would do is get back into arranging and really study and work at that. But the public changed that when I got here. And I'm glad.
